# mutator

Mutation testing for Clojure, Java, Go, TypeScript, Rust, and Python. One run detects the language of each source file, applies that language's mutation rules, and writes the snapshot [uml-viewer](https://github.com/unclebob/uml-viewer) already reads.

Clojure follows [clj-mutate](https://github.com/unclebob/clj-mutate). Go follows [mutate4go](https://github.com/unclebob/mutate4go). Java follows [mutate4java](https://github.com/unclebob/mutate4java). TypeScript, Rust, and Python use the same decisions as Java, spelled in that language. Function names and namespaces come from [crapper](https://github.com/unclebob/crapper), which is what uml-viewer joins to `.metrics/crap.edn`.

A mutant is killed when the tests fail or time out. It survives when the tests still pass. A site on a line the coverage report does not hit is uncovered and is not run. The score uml-viewer paints is killed / (killed + survived).

## Run

```bash
./mutator
```

The first run creates `.venv` and installs the tool. crapper has to be checked out next to this directory (`../crapper`), because that is where the namespace and function names come from. From a project root the tool walks the tree, skips `test`, `spec`, `vendor`, `node_modules`, and `target`, and writes `.metrics/mutate/<namespace>.edn`.

The first run of a tree executes every covered mutant. Start with the file you are working on.

```bash
./mutator src/demo/core.clj          # one file, or a directory
./mutator --scan src/demo           # list sites, do not run tests
./mutator --changed                 # git additions and edits
./mutator --mutate-all              # rerun killed mutants too
./mutator --no-coverage             # do not skip uncovered lines
./mutator --use-existing-coverage   # read reports already on disk
./mutator --test-command "pytest -q tests/test_demo.py"
./mutator --max-workers 3 src/demo/core.clj
```

Once a snapshot exists, the next run is differential. It reruns survivors and every site in a function whose text changed. Killed mutants in an unchanged function stay killed. `--since-last-run` is that same selection. `--mutate-all` ignores it.

Exit `0` when every executed mutant was killed. Exit `2` when the baseline tests fail. Exit `3` when a mutant survives. A failed baseline does not rewrite the snapshot.

## Workers

Mutants of one file run at the same time. The default is one worker per core. `--max-workers` sets the cap. The run uses the smaller of that cap, the number of cores, and

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
ROOT=$PWD; SEEDS=${1:-1,2}; OPS=${2:-1500}; shift 2 2>/dev/null
declare -A PORT=( [node-ts]=3201 [deno]=3202 [php]=3203 [python]=3204 [rust]=3206 )

  for _ in $(seq 1 240); do curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:$p/health" >/dev/null && break; sleep 0.5; done
  targets+=(--target "$b=http://127.0.0.1:$p")

Once a snapshot exists, the next run is differential. It reruns survivors and every site in a function whose text changed. Killed mutants in an unchanged function stay killed. `--since-last-run` is that same selection. `--mutate-all` ignores it.

Exit `0` when every executed mutant was killed. Exit `2` when the baseline tests fail. Exit `3` when a mutant survives. A failed baseline does not rewrite the snapshot.

## Workers

Mutants of one file run at the same time. The default is one worker per core. `--max-workers` sets the cap. The run uses the smaller of that cap, the number of cores, and the number of selected sites. Files are still taken one at a time.

Each worker is a directory under `target/mutation-workers`. The file being mutated is a private copy. A module that reaches that file through a relative import is copied too, so Node resolves the import to the private copy. The rest of the tree is linked. The original files stay as they are. The overlay is removed when that file's mutants finish.

| Python | the dotted module path, or `module.Class` | the function or method name |

#!/bin/sh
# Run the mutation tool, creating a local virtualenv on first use.
ROOT=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
PY="$ROOT/.venv/bin/python"
if [ ! -x "$PY" ]; then
  python3 -m venv "$ROOT/.venv"
  "$ROOT/.venv/bin/pip" install -e "$ROOT"
fi
exec "$PY" -m mutator "$@"
# crapper

CRAP scores for Clojure, Java, Go, TypeScript, Rust, and Python. One run detects the language of each source file, applies that language's complexity and coverage rules, and writes the snapshot [uml-viewer](https://github.com/unclebob/uml-viewer) already reads.

The formula is the one from [crap4clj](https://github.com/unclebob/crap4clj), [crap4java](https://github.com/unclebob/crap4java), and [crap4go](https://github.com/unclebob/crap4go):

```text
CRAP = CC² × (1 − coverage)³ + CC
```

`CC` is cyclomatic complexity. `coverage` is the fraction of the function exercised by tests. A score of 1–5 is low risk, 5–30 is worth a look, and 30+ is complex and under-tested.

## Run

```bash
./crapper
```

The first run creates `.venv` and installs the tool. From a project root it walks the tree, skips `test`, `spec`, `vendor`, `node_modules`, and `target`, and writes two results:

- a table on stdout, worst score first
- `.metrics/crap.edn`, replaced on every successful analysis

```bash
./crapper --no-coverage                  # complexity only; coverage is N/A
./crapper --use-existing-coverage        # read reports already on disk
./crapper src/demo/core.clj src/ui       # these files and trees
./crapper --changed                      # git additions and edits
./crapper combat                         # path fragment, same idea as crap4clj
./crapper --threshold 30                 # exit 2 when the worst score is higher

cat > evidence/redteam.mutation.md <<'E'
# Red team: mutation testing

Tool: Uncle Bob's [mutator](https://github.com/unclebob/mutator) (+ `crapper` checked out beside it), read before running. It was run on **scratch copies** of the backends, never in the repo, so nothing under `backends/` was touched (no `.metrics/` or `target/` created there). Flags: `--no-coverage` (no c8/coverage tooling installed, so every site runs, none are skipped as uncovered), `--max-workers 3`. Raw logs: `evidence/redteam.mutation.node-ts.log`, `evidence/redteam.mutation.python.log`.

| Target | Test command | Mutants | Killed | Survived | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `backends/node-ts/src/domain` (note, precondition, validation) | `npm test --prefix backends/node-ts` | 43 | 42 | 1 | 97.7% |
| `backends/python/domain.py` | `python3 -m unittest discover -s backends/python/tests` | 19 | 17 | 2 | 89.5% |

Caveat (python): the tool's symlink overlay only redirects JS relative imports. The Python test does `sys.path.insert(0, dirname(__file__)/..)`, which resolves through the symlink to the real, unmutated `domain.py`, so the first run showed a false 0% (19/19 survived). The scratch copy of the test was changed to use `os.getcwd()/backends/python` so the overlay is imported. Only the scratch copy was edited. The repo test is untouched.

Only the unit suites were run by the tool. Survivors were then checked against the conformance suite by hand (below).

## Survivors (findings about weak tests)

1. **node-ts `domain/validation.ts:61`, `||` -> `&&`** in `validateCreate`'s `if (errors.length > 0 || title === undefined || body === undefined)`. Not an equivalent mutant: with `&&`, a create with a valid title and an invalid body (e.g. `{"title":"t","body":5}`) returns `ok:true` with `body: undefined`. No node-ts unit test sends a valid title with an invalid body to `validateCreate`. **Killed by conformance**: I applied the mutant to a scratch copy and ran `conformance/run.mjs`: 12 more cases failed than baseline (validate-*, formats-code-points, pin-*, readonly-and-null-bodies). So the HTTP-level suite covers it, but the unit suite does not.
2. **python `domain.py:48`, `>` -> `>=`** in `_check_body` (`len(v) > BODY_MAX`). No test at the exact boundary (100,000 characters must be accepted). Unit tests only try 100,001. **Conformance does not catch it either**: `cases.json` has only `<repeat:100001:b>` for body length, and no 100,000-character case. A real gap in both suites (title has 200/201 boundary cases; body only has the reject side). Applies to every backend.
3. **python `domain.py:30`, `False` -> `True`** in `_encodable` (the `except UnicodeEncodeError` branch). Nothing tests a lone surrogate (`"\ud800"`) in title or body, which the Python backend rejects with 422. `cases.json` has no lone-surrogate case. Related fuzzer finding: node-ts accepts `{"title":"\ud800"}` (201) and the stored value comes back changed, while Python rejects it. The spec does not say which is right, so this behaviour is not pinned by any test.

## Not run
- `store.ts` / `http.ts` (node-ts), the Rust/PHP/Deno backends: the tool was scoped to the pure cores as asked. The fallback `redteam/mutate.mjs` was not needed because `mutator` ran in under a minute.
- Uncovered-site filtering (coverage) was disabled, so the score counts every mutation site.
E

cd ~/Projects/project; cat > redteam/README.md <<'E'
# Red team

Goal: not "the service is perfect", but "under stated conditions it cannot fail in these specific ways", plus evidence that the tests can detect defects.

## Threat model
Attacker is any HTTP client on the wire: unauthenticated, bad token, a legitimate user of the other team (carol vs team-red), or a teammate racing another teammate. Capabilities: arbitrary paths, methods, headers (`If-Match`, `Content-Type`, `Authorization`), bodies (unicode, huge, wrong types, extra/read-only fields, `__proto__`), and parallel requests. Out of scope: network-level attacks, TLS, token theft/guessing, DoS/performance, anything beyond static seeded tokens.

## Invariants ("cannot fail in these ways")
Conditions: one server process, one SQLite file, seeded users (alice/bob on team-red, carol on team-blue), HTTP/1.1, fresh DB.
- **I1** no 5xx for any request sequence.
- **I2** every 4xx is `application/problem+json` with `status` equal to the HTTP status.
- **I3** carol never gets 2xx on a team-red path and never sees a team-red note id in any response body.
- **I4** a note's version never decreases; every 200 PATCH is +1; a 412/428 PATCH leaves stored state untouched (re-GET). Restore of a deleted note is +1, of a live note is +0.
- **I5** no lost update: a PATCH whose If-Match is stale, future, weak, `*`, missing or garbage is never applied. Under concurrency, 16 parallel PATCHes with the same If-Match yield exactly one 200 and fifteen 412, and the final version is v+1.
- **I6** deleted notes are never returned by GET or the live list, and always appear in `?archived=true` for team members until restored.
- **I7** `ETag == "<body.version>"` on every note response.
- **I8** no 2xx without a valid token, except `/health`.
- **M** (model agreement): expected status per ADR-0003 precedence (401, 404, 415, 413, 400/422, 428, 412), trimmed titles, list contents versus the fuzzer's own model.

"Checked" means evaluated after every response in a random sequence (seeded mulberry32 PRNG; the seed and request lines are printed) plus a deterministic probe sweep of ~40 hostile paths x 6 methods x 3 callers per run. This is evidence by search, not a proof: absence of violations over N ops is not exhaustive.

## Run
```
redteam/run-all.sh 1,2 1500            # starts all 5 backends (ports 3201-3206, fresh DB, own process group), fuzzes, stops them
redteam/run-all.sh 1,2 1500 python     # one backend
node redteam/invariants.mjs --target node-ts=http://127.0.0.1:3201 --seed 7 --ops 2000   # against any running server
```
Output: `evidence/redteam.invariants.{json,md}`. Exit 1 if any violation. The "sequence touching the note" printed per violation is the slice of the log that touched that note (a causal slice, not an automatically delta-debugged minimum). Repro = same seed against a fresh server.

Mutation testing: see `evidence/redteam.mutation.md` (Uncle Bob's `mutator`, run on scratch copies).

## Judgement calls built into the oracle
Behaviours the spec does not pin are treated as "invariants only": duplicate or case-variant `archived` query params, `?archived=` (empty), an If-Match list that contains the current ETag, duplicate JSON keys, lone surrogates, `HEAD`/`OPTIONS`, junk team ids in the URL. Observed divergence between backends on these is reported, not failed.

## Not proven
- Performance or behaviour under real network conditions (slow clients, resets, keep-alive reuse, proxies, HTTP/2). Only loopback HTTP/1.1, one connection per request.
- Multi-process or multi-host SQLite on every runtime (the burst test is 16 in-flight requests to a single server process; PHP's built-in server and the others were not tested with several workers on one file).
- Auth beyond the three static tokens: no token rotation, expiry, membership changes (Tier 3), or timing side channels.
- Tier 3 (teams, tags, search, paging) is not modelled.
- The mutation run covers only the pure domain cores with unit tests, not `store`/`http` layers or the Rust/PHP/Deno backends.
E
rm -f /tmp/rt-*.txt /tmp/rt-*.pid; ls redteam evidence | grep -i redteam; for p in 3201 3202 3203 3204 3206 3291 3292; do ss -ltn | grep ":$p " ; done; ls backends/*/ -d >/dev/null; find backends -maxdepth 2 \( -name .metrics -o -name mutation-workers \) | head; date

input.message:
Red team finished. The fuzzer ran on all 5 backends (2 seeds × 1500 ops, about 2,800 requests per run). Only node-ts violated an invariant. Both mutator runs found weak tests.

**Invariants (`evidence/redteam.invariants.{md,json}`)**
- **node-ts, I1 (5xx):** `GET //` and `HEAD //` return 500 for every caller (about 27 per seed). In an earlier run `/notes/%E0` and `/teams/%E0/notes` also returned 500 with a valid token; they came back clean in the last run, so I can't say whether that was fixed.
- **node-ts, M:** a title of `"\ud800"` (lone surrogate) is accepted with 201, but later reads return a different title. Python rejects it. Seen at seed 2, op 15. Repro: `node redteam/invariants.mjs --target node-ts=URL --seed 2 --ops 1500`.
- **deno, php, python, rust:** zero violations of I1–I8. The 16-way same-If-Match burst gave exactly one 200 on all 10 runs.
- **Unpinned divergences (not counted as violations):**
  - `?archived=` gives 200 on node-ts and 422 on the other backends.
  - Earlier runs: an If-Match list containing the current ETag was accepted by deno, php and python but not by node-ts or rust. Duplicate `archived` params resolve first-wins vs last-wins differently across backends.

**Mutation (`evidence/redteam.mutation.md`)**
- I used Uncle Bob's `mutator` on scratch copies. Nothing was written under `backends/`.
- **node-ts domain:** 42 of 43 killed (97.7%). The survivor is `validation.ts:61`, `||` → `&&`. Unit tests don't catch it, but conformance fails 12 more cases with it applied.
- **python `domain.py`:** 17 of 19 killed (89.5%). Two survivors are gaps in both suites:
  - `>` → `>=` at the 100,000-character body limit. No case tests exactly 100,000.
  - Lone-surrogate rejection is untested.
- **Python caveat:** mutator's overlay only redirects JS imports, so the first Python run showed a false 0%. I fixed the scratch copy of the test and reran.

**Not done**
- I did not write the fallback `redteam/mutate.mjs`, because mutator ran.
- The "minimal failing sequence" printed per violation is a log slice that touched the offending note, not a delta-debugged minimum.

**Files:** `redteam/invariants.mjs`, `redteam/run-all.sh`, `redteam/README.md`, `evidence/redteam.mutation.node-ts.log`, `evidence/redteam.mutation.python.log`, plus the evidence files above.
